title: Sensitive Telemetry Escrow and Role‑Bound Reveal Workflow
creator: Marisol Gomez
description:
Background: As telemetry volume grows and more customers enable detailed tracing and debug-level logs, we've had repeated requests for fine-grained, auditable controls that let platform operators see unredacted events only when strictly authorized. Current scrubbing is static and irreversible, which blocks incident investigations and increases support MTTR for enterprise customers who need just-in-time access under governance.

Goal: Implement an "escrow and reveal" pattern for sensitive telemetry where sensitive fields are stored in an encrypted escrow, access to reveal is bound to RBAC + approval workflow, and all access is recorded in an immutable audit ledger. The feature must cover traces (span attributes), structured logs, and high-cardinality error payloads that feed latency/error dashboards. It must preserve existing SLOs (target: p99 latency + <=5% ingestion overhead) and be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Traces: span tags/attributes (user identifiers, email, prompt inputs) routed through a tracing hook that marks and envelopes sensitive attributes.
- Logs: structured JSON logs tagged by pipeline classifier; sensitive keys are escrowed.
- Dashboards: latency/error dashboards continue to show aggregated metrics; drill‑down to raw events requires reveal permission.

Success criteria:
1) Administrators can request reveal for a specific event/span via Console or API; reveals are logged and link to an approval event.
2) No plaintext sensitive field is written to long-term indexable storage without an access-granted event.
3) Reveal flow enforces RBAC, optional two-step approval for high-risk tenants, and time-bounded access (e.g., 30 minutes).
4) End-to-end tests and load tests prove ingestion overhead <5% and read-latency degradation <10% for drilldowns.

Notes: We'll use envelope encryption (tenant-scoped ephemeral KMS keys) for escrow store to minimize blast radius and to enable tenant-specific purging/rotation.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks can tag and envelope sensitive span attributes before they hit the main trace index (unit tests + integration).
Logs pipeline includes classifier + escrow step; nothing in the primary log index contains unmasked PII by default.
Console UI: admin can open a reveal request tied to a tenant/event; the request shows approver, justification, and TTL for reveal.
Audit ledger shows: requestor, approver(s), timestamp, event id, fields revealed, and ephemeral key id. Ledger is append-only and immutable.
Performance: pipeline CPU overhead <5% at typical QPS; trace ingest latency p99 increases <5ms in worst-case.
technical_notes: Tracing hooks: add pre-ingest hook in the collector that tags span attributes with sensitivity labels from a schema (artifact: repo/specs/telemetry-sensitivity.md).
Escrow store: new S3/GCS-backed encrypted store with envelope keys; metadata index stores pointer + fingerprint (SHA256) of preserved fields.
Encryption: tenant-scoped DEK encrypted by platform KEK; for Dedicated/Private, support customer KMS (bring-your-own-key).
Classifier: hybrid approach — regex + ML model for edge cases. Classifier runs in the pipeline and emits "sensitivity:high/med/low" tag for each message.

Access flow: Console/API -> Create reveal request -> Auto-approve for platform-admins OR route to on-call approvers for high-risk tenants -> Reveal service decrypts and streams plaintext to auditor session for TTL window.
Store ephemeral decrypted payload in memory-only caches; forbid writes of decrypted content back to long-term indices.
Audit ledger: append-only object in write-once storage with HMAC chain to detect tampering; replicate ledger separately for HA.
Retention: policy tiers (transient=7d, standard=30d, long=180d). Purge job removes escrow objects and metadata; for Private, provide a playbook for physical media destruction.
Compatibility: runtime agents (python/go/log4j wrappers) need a small SDK to annotate telemetry before sending to collector. Backwards compatibility mode present to avoid breaking older agents.
rollout_plan: MVP (Phase 1) - opt-in tenant list: implement tracing hooks + escrow store + basic Console reveal flow; internal rollout to SRE and 3 pilot customers (4 weeks).
Phase 2 - RBAC + approvals: integrate with SSO/SCIM, add two-step approvals for high-risk tenants, and add audit ledger hardening (6 weeks).
Phase 3 - Performance tuning & model improvements: reduce classifier false positives, optimize encryption/decryption hot-paths, and expand to Dedicated/Private KMS options (4 weeks).
Migration: write migration tasks to backfill sensitivity tags for historical data (best-effort), mark all historical high-risk fields for escrow with a TTL of 30 days before deletion.
qa_notes: Unit tests for classifier and tracing hook logic must simulate edge-case payloads (nested JSON, base64 blobs, long strings).
Integration canary: route 1% of production traffic through escrow pipeline and compare metrics/latency with baseline.
Security tests: key rotation, KMS permissions validation, ledger tamper simulation, and privilege escalation attempts audit.
